Cloud Spanner requires provisioned nodes and lacks mobile SDKs. Cloud SQL is a server-side relational database without built-in offline sync or real-time push. Bigtable requires always-on nodes and is designed for server-side analytics, not mobile client access.

ul.li: Firestore's serverless pricing model charges per document operation, so development and testing environments with minimal traffic cost nearly nothing — ideal for startups iterating on their mobile app.

Firestore Security Rules provide declarative, server-enforced access control keyed to authenticated users, enabling direct client-to-database access without a custom backend for basic CRUD operations.
Real-time listeners use an efficient snapshot-diff protocol, pushing only changed fields to connected clients rather than the full document, minimizing mobile bandwidth consumption.
Offline writes are queued locally and reconciled with the server when connectivity returns; Firestore handles conflict resolution using a last-writer-wins strategy with server timestamps.

question.title: Database Selection: IoT Time Series
question.scenario: An industrial IoT platform needs to ingest millions of sensor readings per second and run analytical queries over petabytes of historical data.
question.question-text: Which database is optimized for high-volume time-series data ingestion and analytical queries?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: The wide-column NoSQL database designed for millions of writes per second at consistent low latency and efficient range scans over petabytes of time-series data is the right choice here.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Cloud Bigtable is optimized for high-throughput writes and efficient range scans, making it the best GCP database for time-series IoT data at scale. It ingests millions of operations per second with consistent sub-10ms latency, stores petabytes of data, and integrates with analytics tools like BigQuery (via federation), Dataflow, and Dataproc for downstream processing. Cloud SQL cannot handle millions of writes per second. Firestore is designed for mobile/web document workloads, not high-throughput telemetry. Cloud Spanner provides global consistency at higher cost but is not optimized for the append-heavy, scan-heavy pattern of time-series analytics.

ul.li: Row key design for time-series should avoid monotonic timestamps (which create hotspots); techniques include salting with a hash prefix, using reverse timestamps, or prepending the sensor/device ID to distribute writes across tablets.

Different column families within the same Bigtable table can have different garbage collection policies, allowing raw high-frequency data to expire after 30 days while hourly aggregates are retained for years.
BigQuery can query Bigtable data directly using federated external tables, enabling SQL analytics over live Bigtable data without ETL — ideal for ad-hoc investigation of IoT anomalies.
Bigtable performance scales linearly by adding nodes; a 10-node cluster handles roughly 100,000 rows/sec, while a 100-node cluster handles approximately 1 million rows/sec.

question.title: Database Selection: High-Performance PostgreSQL
question.scenario: A company has a complex PostgreSQL application with OLTP and OLAP queries. They need better performance than Cloud SQL provides while maintaining PostgreSQL compatibility.
question.question-text: Which service provides PostgreSQL compatibility with enhanced performance for mixed transactional and analytical workloads?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: The GCP database that maintains full PostgreSQL wire compatibility while adding a built-in columnar engine for analytics and a high-performance storage layer for transactions is the best fit for mixed OLTP/OLAP workloads.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL is purpose-built for demanding PostgreSQL workloads that blend transactional (OLTP) and analytical (OLAP) queries. Its columnar engine automatically accelerates analytical queries without ETL, while its adaptive storage and caching system optimizes transactional throughput beyond what standard PostgreSQL or Cloud SQL can deliver. It maintains full PostgreSQL compatibility, including extensions and PL/pgSQL. Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL runs standard PostgreSQL without the columnar engine. Cloud Spanner's PostgreSQL interface supports only a subset of PostgreSQL syntax. BigQuery is an analytics warehouse that does not handle OLTP workloads.

ul.li: AlloyDB's columnar engine automatically identifies frequently queried columns and materializes them in a columnar format in memory, accelerating analytical queries up to 100x without requiring explicit materialized views or ETL.

Cloud Spanner's PostgreSQL interface lacks full compatibility — it does not support PostgreSQL extensions (e.g., PostGIS, pg_trgm), stored procedures in PL/pgSQL, or advisory locks that complex applications depend on.

AlloyDB separates compute from a distributed, log-structured storage layer, enabling independent scaling of read pool instances and the primary — a fundamental architectural advantage over Cloud SQL's coupled compute-storage model.
For pure analytics without transactional requirements, BigQuery is more cost-effective; AlloyDB's value is in workloads where OLTP and OLAP queries run against the same dataset without data movement.

question.title: Storage Selection: Static Website
question.scenario: A company needs to host static files (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images) for a website with global users.
question.question-text: Which storage solution is most appropriate for hosting static website content globally?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Cloud Storage can serve static website content directly from a bucket, and pairing it with Cloud CDN caches assets at global edge locations for low-latency delivery worldwide.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Cloud Storage provides built-in static website hosting from a bucket, serving HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images over HTTP. Combined with Cloud CDN, assets are cached at Google's global edge points of presence, delivering low-latency responses to users worldwide. This is a cost-effective, serverless solution requiring no server management. Persistent Disk is block storage for VMs and cannot serve HTTP. Cloud SQL is a relational database. Filestore is NFS storage that requires VMs to serve content — adding unnecessary infrastructure complexity and cost.

ul.li: Static website hosting is configured by setting the MainPageSuffix (e.g., index.html) and NotFoundPage (e.g., 404.html) properties on the bucket, enabling automatic routing of requests.
For HTTPS support and custom domains, place a Cloud Load Balancer in front of the Cloud Storage bucket with a managed SSL certificate; the load balancer also integrates with Cloud CDN.

Firebase Hosting is an alternative that provides additional features like easy CLI deployment, automatic SSL, preview channels for staging, and atomic deploys — consider it for teams already using Firebase.
Cloud CDN cache invalidation allows purging stale content after deployments; combining CDN with versioned file names (e.g., app.v2.js) provides instant updates without cache purge delays.

question.title: Storage Selection: Media Rendering
question.scenario: A media company's rendering farm needs shared storage accessible by hundreds of VMs simultaneously for reading input files and writing output.
question.question-text: Which storage solution provides high-performance shared file access for compute-intensive workloads?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Filestore High Scale (Zonal) tier provides high-throughput NFS storage designed for HPC and rendering workloads where hundreds of VMs need simultaneous read-write access to shared files.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Filestore High Scale tier (formerly Zonal) delivers high-throughput NFS storage purpose-built for compute-intensive workloads like media rendering, genomics pipelines, and HPC simulations. It supports simultaneous read-write access from hundreds of clients with throughput scaling into tens of GB/s. Cloud Storage has higher per-operation latency and lacks POSIX semantics needed by rendering software. Persistent Disk multi-attach only supports read-only mode, preventing render workers from writing output. Local SSD is per-VM ephemeral storage with no sharing capability.

ul.li: Filestore High Scale can deliver up to 26 GB/s aggregate throughput, sufficient for rendering farms where hundreds of worker VMs read large texture and geometry files simultaneously.
Persistent Disk multi-attach allows connecting a single disk to up to 10 VMs but in read-only mode only, making it unsuitable for rendering workflows that must write output frames to shared storage.

Higher Filestore capacity provisions higher baseline throughput; for burst-heavy rendering jobs, over-provisioning capacity is a common strategy to ensure sufficient I/O headroom during peak rendering passes.

For rendering farms that stage input from Cloud Storage, a common pattern is to pre-load assets onto Filestore before a render job and copy completed frames back to Cloud Storage for long-term archival.

question.title: Storage Selection: Data Lake
question.scenario: A company is building a data lake to store raw data from multiple sources in various formats for future analytics processing.
question.question-text: Which storage solution is most appropriate for a data lake storing diverse data formats at scale?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about whether the scenario needs to grow by adding more units or by making existing units bigger.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Cloud Storage is the natural foundation for a data lake on Google Cloud. It stores any data format (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, images, video) at unlimited scale with 11-nines durability and strong consistency. It integrates directly with analytics services: BigQuery for SQL queries via external tables, Dataflow for stream and batch ETL, and Dataproc for Spark/Hadoop processing. Storage class tiering (Standard to Archive) optimizes cost as data ages. Bigtable is a NoSQL database for structured key-value data. Persistent Disk is block storage for VMs. Cloud SQL is a relational database — none are designed for format-agnostic data lake storage.

ul.li: BigQuery can query Parquet, ORC, Avro, CSV, and JSON files directly in Cloud Storage using external or BigLake tables, enabling SQL analytics without loading data into BigQuery's managed storage.

Using columnar formats like Parquet or Avro for data lake files dramatically improves query performance and reduces cost because analytics engines can read only the needed columns and leverage compression.

Object Lifecycle Management policies can automatically tier older data from Standard to Nearline to Coldline to Archive, reducing storage costs for historical data that is queried less frequently over time.

Cloud Storage's flat namespace and strong consistency simplify data lake management — there are no directory-lock contention issues, and newly written files are immediately visible to all analytics jobs.

question.title: Database Selection: Financial Ledger
question.scenario: A fintech company needs a database for their core banking ledger that requires ACID transactions, SQL support, and the ability to serve customers globally with strong consistency guarantees.
question.question-text: Which database is most appropriate for a globally distributed financial ledger requiring strong consistency?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: A globally distributed financial ledger demands externally consistent ACID transactions across continents — the only GCP database providing this guarantee with SQL and horizontal scaling is the right answer.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Cloud Spanner is uniquely suited for global financial ledgers because it provides external consistency — the strongest isolation level — guaranteeing that transactions appear to execute sequentially even when running across continents. This prevents double-spending, balance discrepancies, and audit inconsistencies that weaker consistency models would allow. Firestore is a NoSQL document database without SQL joins or the relational model financial systems require. Cloud SQL cross-region replicas use asynchronous replication, so they cannot provide strong consistency globally. AlloyDB is regional only and does not support global distribution.

ul.li: Spanner's TrueTime API provides globally meaningful, monotonically increasing commit timestamps, enabling auditors to reconstruct the exact global ordering of every ledger transaction across all regions.

Cloud SQL cross-region read replicas use asynchronous replication with potential seconds of lag; for a financial ledger, this lag could cause a balance read in one region to miss a recent debit committed in another — an unacceptable inconsistency.

Multi-region Spanner provides 99.999% availability (five nines), meaning less than 5.3 minutes of downtime per year — critical for financial systems with strict uptime SLAs and regulatory requirements.

AlloyDB offers excellent PostgreSQL performance for mixed workloads but operates within a single region; it cannot serve a global customer base with consistent, low-latency transactions the way Spanner can.

question.title: Storage Selection: Compliance Archive
question.scenario: A healthcare organization must store patient records for 10 years to meet regulatory requirements. The data is rarely accessed but must be protected against accidental or malicious deletion.
question.question-text: Which Cloud Storage configuration ensures data cannot be deleted before the retention period expires?

choices.choice: Archive storage class with retention policy and bucket lock
Coldline storage with IAM deny policies

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: For regulatory compliance requiring guaranteed 10-year retention with deletion protection, combine the lowest-cost storage class with a retention policy locked by bucket lock to make it permanent and irreversible.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The correct configuration combines Archive storage (lowest cost for rarely accessed data), a retention policy set to the required 10-year duration, and bucket lock to make that policy permanent and irrevocable. Once locked, no user — including project owners and organization admins — can delete objects before the retention period expires, satisfying HIPAA and other healthcare compliance requirements. Standard storage with versioning does not prevent deletion. Nearline with lifecycle rules automates deletion, the opposite of preservation. Coldline with IAM deny policies can be overridden by sufficiently privileged administrators.

ul.li: Bucket lock is a one-time, irreversible operation — once applied, the retention policy cannot be removed, shortened, or modified for the lifetime of the bucket; thorough testing with an unlocked policy is essential first.

Object holds (event-based and temporary) can be layered on top of retention policies for additional protection, useful for placing litigation holds on specific patient records without affecting the entire bucket.

IAM deny policies can restrict deletion permissions but can be modified or removed by organization administrators, so they do not provide the same immutability guarantee as bucket lock for regulatory compliance.

Archive storage class has a 365-day minimum storage duration charge, but for 10-year retention this is irrelevant; the cost savings over Coldline (90-day minimum) or Nearline (30-day minimum) accumulate significantly over a decade.

term.name: Cloud SQL
term.definition: Fully managed relational database service for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.
term.exam-note: Best for regional relational workloads with standard SQL requirements.

term.name: Cloud Spanner
term.definition: Globally distributed, horizontally scalable relational database with strong consistency and SQL support.
term.exam-note: Choose for global-scale applications requiring strong consistency and SQL.

term.name: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
term.definition: Fully managed PostgreSQL-compatible database with enhanced performance for transactional and analytical workloads.
term.exam-note: Offers up to 4x faster transactions and 100x faster analytics than standard PostgreSQL.

term.name: Firestore
term.definition: Serverless document database with real-time synchronization, offline support, and automatic scaling.
term.exam-note: Best for mobile and web apps needing offline support and real-time sync.

term.name: Cloud Bigtable
term.definition: Wide-column NoSQL database for high-throughput, low-latency workloads at petabyte scale.
term.exam-note: Ideal for time-series, IoT, analytics, and workloads requiring consistent sub-10ms latency.

term.name: Memorystore
term.definition: Fully managed in-memory data store service supporting Redis and Memcached.
term.exam-note: Use for caching, session management, and real-time analytics requiring sub-millisecond latency.

term.name: Cloud Storage
term.definition: Object storage service providing 99.999999999% durability for unstructured data.
term.exam-note: Foundation for data lakes, backups, static websites, and any unstructured data storage.

term.name: Storage Classes
term.definition: Cloud Storage tiers (Standard, Nearline, Coldline, Archive) optimized for different access patterns and costs.
term.exam-note: All classes have same durability; differ in cost and minimum storage duration.

term.name: Persistent Disk
term.definition: Network-attached block storage for Compute Engine VMs with automatic replication.
term.exam-note: Data persists independently of VM; supports snapshots and resizing without downtime.

term.name: Local SSD
term.definition: High-performance ephemeral storage physically attached to the VM host server.
term.exam-note: Data is lost when VM stops; use for caches, temporary processing, or scratch space.

term.name: Hyperdisk
term.definition: Block storage with independently provisionable and dynamically adjustable IOPS and throughput.
term.exam-note: Provides highest performance and flexibility for demanding workloads.

term.name: Filestore
term.definition: Fully managed NFS file server service for applications requiring shared file systems.
term.exam-note: Choose for workloads needing POSIX file system semantics and shared access.

term.name: Signed URL
term.definition: Time-limited URL providing access to Cloud Storage objects without requiring authentication.
term.exam-note: Use for sharing objects with external users without giving them Google accounts.

term.name: Retention Policy
term.definition: Cloud Storage policy specifying minimum duration that objects must be retained.
term.exam-note: Combine with bucket lock to make retention permanent for compliance requirements.

term.name: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK)
term.definition: Encryption using keys stored in Cloud KMS that customers create and manage.
term.exam-note: Provides key rotation control, audit logging, and ability to revoke access.
